content:
Fiona, a beloved Nile hippopotamus at the Cincinnati Zoo, died Thursday after ingesting a hat that fell into her habitat by accident last week.

Zoo staff made multiple attempts to remove the hat, but were unsuccessful.

“We know everyone in the community will be crushed by this news, as we all are,” a post from the zoo read. “Please keep her keepers and everyone who tried to help her in your thoughts as they try to navigate and come to terms with this shocking news.”

A knit hat mistakenly fell into Fiona’s habitat last week after it was tossed into the air by a visitor and caught by a ceiling fan that threw it into a small opening of the enclosure.

“Our animal care team was heroic in their efforts to save her. They did everything possible, but her body couldn’t fight anymore,” Cincinnati Zoo director Dave Jenike said in a statement. “She was dearly loved by her Zoo family and countless others around the world. Her loss will be felt deeply by so many.”

Veterinarians had been optimistic that Fiona might be able to pass the hat on her own, even borrowing a vibration plate from a horse farm in hopes of moving the hat through her digestive tract. Because she had reached her full-grown size, specialists warned against performing surgery.

The zoo shared consistent updates with the public about Fiona’s care and condition on social media, sharing photos and videos of her receiving treatment.

“Fiona was such a gift,” Thane Maynard, Cincinnati Zoo executive board chair, sad in a statement. “I have never known an animal so beloved in all my life. From the day she was born, she was like lightning in a bottle. And she will be remembered and beloved many years from now.”

The 9-year-old hippo gained worldwide fame when she was born prematurely in January 2017, just months after the fatal shooting of Harambe, a gorilla at the zoo, after a child accidentally got into his enclosure.

When she was born six weeks early, Fiona weighed only 29 pounds, about 25 pounds below the lowest average hippo birth weight. At the time of her death, she weighed more than 2,500 pounds.

Fiona’s story drew the attention of millions around the world, inspiring children’s books and even a new ice cream flavor.

Ohio Gov.-elect Amy Acton expressed her sadness over the loss of Fiona on Thursday.

“Fiona captured the hearts of millions and became one of Cincinnati’s most beloved icons,” she wrote in a social media post. “Her story brought joy, hope, and a little extra magic to our state.”

The Cincinnati Bengals also paid tribute to Fiona.
